input.quote: 6. DOCUMENTATION AND DISPUTES. Client will be provided upon request with documentation supporting the amount charged (other than the minimum monthly fees listed in Section 4) and will be entitled to contest any charge
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no audit, inspection, records-examination or usage-verification right running against the Client. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records", "verif", "books" and "monitor" return nothing, and the sections where such a right would sit are clean: § 5–6 (Compensation/Documentation and Disputes) gives the verification right to us (TrueLink must support its charges on request and we may contest them), and § 8 (Covenants and Warranties of Client) imposes only compliance, access-restriction and content warranties with no examination right. The only TrueLink self-help right, § 8(f), is limited to implementing technical mechanisms on its own systems to prevent spamming, not access to or inspection of Client systems or records. No obligation on us to submit to audits therefore exists, and nothing sits in walk-away territory (no unlimited, unannounced or remote-access audit). Since the absence of any audit right is more favourable to us than the preferred position, there is nothing to limit and we should not introduce an audit right by redlining. Noted for the record: because there is no audit clause, the usual protective parameters (12-month frequency, 30 days' notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor-borne cost, no system access) are simply not needed; if TrueLink later proposes fee or usage verification, we would insert those limits then.
